content.title: About
content.content: Thin‑crust cheese pizza is a popular fast‑food option made with a crisp, thin dough topped with tomato sauce and melted cheese. It is commonly served in quick‑serve restaurants and pizzerias.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thin crust cooks faster, allowing the pizza to be ready in 2‑3 minutes in a high‑heat oven.
The classic cheese used is mozzarella, but cheddar, parmesan, or a blend are often added.
In Italy, a similar thin pizza is called “pizza di marinara” or “Neapolitan,” though the traditional Neapolitan has a puffier edge.
Cheese pizza is a common vegetarian option because it contains no meat.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cheese, especially mozzarella, is rich in calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Protein rich
items.content: Cheese provides high‑quality animal protein that supports tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 found in dairy supports nervous system function.

items.title: Lower carbohydrate content
items.content: Thin crust typically contains fewer carbs than a traditional thick crust, making it more suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Potential probiotics (when using fermented sauces)
items.content: Some tomato sauces are fermented, adding beneficial bacteria.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Cheese and sauce often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who cannot digest lactose may experience discomfort from dairy ingredients.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey can cause severe reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite the thin crust, cheese makes the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional dough contains gluten, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheese pizza is usually eaten hot, sliced into wedges. Fresh herbs (basil, oregano) or a light drizzle of hot sauce can be added for extra flavor. For a lighter version, choose whole‑grain or gluten‑free crusts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore the crisp crust.
